newsitem.title: USA: NFA fines Peregine Financial Group Inc $75,000.
newsitem.headline: NFA fines Peregine Financial Group Inc $75,000.

text.p: Peregrine Financial Group Inc was fined $75,000 by the National Futures Association after the self-regulatory agency found the futures commission merchant (FCM) in violation of several rules, the NFA said.
Peregrine neither admitted nor denied the allegations, the NFA said.

The NFA alleged that Peregrine's associated persons (APs) used deceptive and misleading sales practices and promotional material in radio ads, and that Peregrine failed to adequately supervise its APs and their sales manager.
APs solicit orders and customer funds on behalf of an FCM.
"The only thing I have to say is that it's an issue that came up over a year and a half ago and we took corrective action," Russ Wasendorf, president of Peregrine, told Reuters
Wasendorf said Peregrine, which is based in Cedar Falls, Iowa, with offices in Chicago, terminated the supervisors responsible for the ads.
The NFA also found that Peregrine failed to segregate funds to meet capital requirements. On March 3 and March 6, 1995, the firm was undersegregated $554,000 and $73,000, respectively.
The NFA said Peregrine failed to correctly calculate segregated funds. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
